answer: In an EigenTrust-style network, reputation decays exponentially with a defined half-life, so past endorsements lose weight unless renewed through sustained honest service. Reciprocity-weighted transitivity limits the influence of unsupported or one-way ratings. Newly spawned identities—whether named walnut, bridge, or cedar—have few trusted paths and near-zero eigenvector centrality; without accumulated credible feedback, they cannot meet consensus thresholds or rapidly manufacture influence.
